packs.title: Umbrellas, Ruins and New Steps
packs.promise: Find another Budapest in the spaces beneath umbrellas, above ruined walls and between a garden’s growing surfaces.

q.s: Collect the shapes that fit between four bronze umbrellas.
st: From a comfortable stopped viewpoint or the official image, choose three different gaps: beneath an umbrella rim, between two figures and beside an arm or coat.
Describe each gap using a shape word or small outline. Look at the surrounding space rather than inventing a story about the people represented.
Place your three gaps in an order from narrowest-looking to widest-looking. Save the shapes and the order; no measurement or walk around the group is required.

q.s: Collect a near edge, a reflected shape and a farther layer.
st: From a stopped place back from the pond, collect one near border, one reflected or overlapping shape, and one layer farther behind. Use the official image if glare, weather or access makes the layers hard to see.
Name what lets you distinguish each layer: a border, an upside-down shape, a color contrast or an overlap. No botanical names are needed.
Save three observations in near-to-far order. Keep every plant and animal where it is.

q.s: Make a tiny design for greenery that grows into the air.
st: Look at a planted upright surface and a supporting line in the hanging-garden structure, or use the official park photograph. Notice where greenery meets metal.
Invent a small garden of your own for a blank upright panel. Sketch two planted zones and one deliberate open gap, or describe their arrangement in words.
Give your design a title and save the two zones and gap. This is a private sketch, not a proposal to alter the park or a claim about its planting.

packs.title: Riverlines and Park Rhythms
packs.promise: Find Budapest in a changing view, a repeating shape and a quiet moment.

q.s: Collect three repeats in the front of Pesti Vigadó.
st: Choose a comfortable public spot in Vigadó tér with a view of Pesti Vigadó, keeping its entrances clear.
Find a repeated window shape, a repeated vertical division and a smaller repeated ornament on the facade. Choose details you can see without approaching the building.
Turn each repeat into a pattern of short and long marks in your note. Let the spacing you see set the rhythm.
Put your three patterns together and choose which one gives the building its strongest beat.

q.s: Give one Danube view a tiny caption of your own.
st: Find a comfortable stopping place on the upper pedestrian promenade beside Vigadó tér. Stay on the pedestrian side of the tram route.
Choose one near detail in the paving or promenade furniture and one distant shape across the river on the Buda hillside.
Write a six-word caption that connects the two. Try one version, then swap a single word to change its mood.
Save your chosen caption and name the near and far details that started it.

q.s: Build a pattern collection at the Museum of Ethnography.
st: Find a ground-level public viewpoint beside the Museum of Ethnography where you can see a curved wing and part of its patterned facade.
Collect three scales of pattern: a small repeated mark, a larger cluster of marks and the broad curve of the building.
For each scale, choose a simple comparison such as a beat, a row or a wave. Describe what you actually see without needing to name the motif.
Save the three comparisons in order from smallest to largest.
